title: Narrow opt-in silence-is-consent with a deterministic timeout
action: Plan Phase 4, second half (per c706053e): a NARROW opt-in silence-is-consent mode. Default OFF, and off means the code path does not exist at runtime. Read `supervisor.consent` from .bee/config.json through the existing notify_enabled config seam: an object {enabled: bool, timeout_seconds: number}; enabled defaults to false, and a malformed or missing value is read as OFF (fail closed — the opposite of the notify default, because a wrong guess here auto-proceeds instead of merely staying quiet). Scope is the whole point and is enforced as a named predicate, not an inline condition: consent applies ONLY to a queued non-gate ask — a mailbox row of kind intervention that sup-8 stamped queued while the human is away. It NEVER applies to a gate, never to kind urgent, never to kind escalation, and never to a one-way-door low-confidence ask; give that predicate its own function and its own test naming each excluded case. The timeout lives in the DETERMINISTIC layer, never the model: add `bee supervisor consent-sweep [--json]`, a pure tick that reads the clock once, auto-proceeds every eligible queued row whose age exceeds timeout_seconds, and returns the ids it proceeded. Every auto-proceed leaves two marks: the row is stamped consented_at with the timeout that applied, and one decision is logged through the existing decision-log path naming the row, the point-key, and the elapsed time — an auto-proceed that left no record is the failure mode this whole mode is judged on. Render it PROMINENTLY in the sup-9 WakeReport: an auto-proceeded row takes the FIRST line of 'What needs you' with a marker that reads unmistakably as 'this went ahead without you', ranked above every other item regardless of the sup-9 impact order, and the count also appears in the sup-10 metrics line. Tests in the same tests module: consent off (default, missing key, malformed value) sweeps nothing; a gate ask, an urgent row and an escalation row are each refused by name; an eligible row younger than the timeout is untouched; an eligible row older is proceeded, stamped, and logged exactly once; a second sweep does not re-proceed it; the WakeReport puts the auto-proceeded row first with its marker. Regen deferred to the wave barrier.

truths: a gate, an urgent row and an escalation row are each refused by the consent predicate by name
every auto-proceed stamps the row and logs exactly one decision, and a second sweep re-proceeds nothing

artifacts.substantive: fail-closed config read, the eligibility predicate, the deterministic sweep, the report marker

key_links: the sweep consumes sup-8's queued rows and its result reaches the sup-9 report and the sup-10 metrics line
prohibitions: no gate or gate-bypass level is ever read or written by this path
the timeout is never supplied by a model
a missing or malformed config value is OFF, never on
